messages:
jordan: heads up — after landing PTQ-8bit for the new reranker (model v2.3.1-ptq) our internal devset NDCG@10 dropped ~4% vs fp16, MRR almost identical. wondering if this is a quantization quality regression or an eval/formatting mismatch. :thinking:

anya: ugh. can you paste the eval command and the metric table?

jordan: sure — run we used:
```
python eval/rerank_eval.py \
  --model checkpoints/v2.3.1-ptq \
  --queries data/dev_queries.jsonl \
  --docs data/dev_docs.jsonl \
  --qfmt truncate:128 \
  --docfmt title+body:512 \
  --batch 64 \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr
```
and the short table:
```
model                 | ndcg@10 | mrr
fp16-v2.3.1           | 0.412   | 0.271
ptq-8bit-v2.3.1       | 0.396   | 0.269
```

mike: small drop but not tiny. did you compare per-query ndcg distribution? could be a long-tail issue (a few queries losing a lot).

jordan: I looked at top-of-distribution — most queries within noise, but ~25 queries drop >0.2 ndcg each.

samir: are you sure the inputs are identical? tokenization/normalization mismatch after export can cause this. PTQ pipeline touched the tokenizer export step last week.

jordan: good call — I re-ran with a deterministic dump of token ids and they match for 99.9% of examples. differences are mainly on very long title concatenations where truncation boundary changes token alignment.

anya: truncation boundary changes can flip doc ranking a bit. try the eval with docfmt "title:64 body:448" and also with full-doc scoring for the top100 to see if truncation explains it.

jordan: will do. also suspicious about softmax temperature changes due to quantization scaling. I dumped logits for a sample of affected queries — fp16 had slightly higher margin between top candidates vs ptq. small but consistent. snippet:
```
# example logits for query q1234 (top3 scores)
fp16: [5.22, 4.31, 3.10]
ptq:  [5.01, 4.05, 3.02]
```

mike: that would reduce NDCG but not MRR if top-1 occasionally swaps. but your MRR is flat — odd. maybe the ranking order within top10 shuffled but top-1 stable?

anya: can we check pairwise swap counts for positions 2-10 between fp16 and ptq? Also check if eval script uses the same tie-breaking. I've seen deterministic tie-breaking differ across runtime exports.

jordan: good point. eval script uses stable_sort by score descending then doc_id. but the model export changed score precision so ties are rare. I'll add a swap diff.

eval-bot: CI eval completed for run 2026-03-18-ptq-sanity: ndcg@10=0.3957 (baseline 0.4120), mrr=0.2691, changed_queries=27, top1_swaps=3.

samir: CI shows changed_queries ~27 — matches your manual check. Top1_swaps low. that aligns with hypothesis: perturbations in mid-rank affecting ndcg more than mrr.

anya: long-term we should add a post-quantization calibration step: temperature scaling or a tiny bias correction layer to recover ranking margins. Before that, do these quick checks:
- reproduce eval with exact same token ids (you did)
- run no-truncate docfmt to rule out truncation artifacts
- evaluate on MS MARCO dev set and the internal dev to see if it's dataset-specific
- do a quantization sweep (8bit symmetric, 8bit asymmetric, 6bit if supported) and measure per-query delta distribution

jordan: plan: I’ll run the no-truncate pass + ms-marco within the next 3 hrs, start a 3-point quant sweep, and produce per-query swap diffs. assigning to me.

mike: add an ablation where you re-run ptq but only quantize the feedforward layers (leave attention in fp16) — sometimes attention is more sensitive for rerankers.

jordan: noted. will add that.

anya: also add a quick eval where you score with fp16 but apply ptq model logits scaled by a learned scalar per-head (cheap sim) — to see if simple linear correction helps without re-quantizing.

jordan: ok will try. if we confirm it's quantization margin compression, we can either: 1) adjust quant params, 2) add tiny downstream calibration, or 3) ship ptq for latency-critical routes but keep fp16 for high-quality routes.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary run for route "search-fast" will use ptq model at 10% traffic in 2h if no regression label posted.

anya: don't ramp until we have the per-query diff and ms-marco sanity. set canary to hold. :eyes:

deploy-bot: canary hold requested — will wait for manual approval.

jordan: updated plan posted to the eval ticket with links to the per-query CSV and scripts. will ping when CI re-run finishes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
